name: IoT Sensor Telemetry Gap-Filling via generate_series and LOCF
description: Industrial IoT sensors emit readings intermittently to save bandwidth. Downstream machine learning models require strict continuous 1-minute time grids with Last Observation Carried Forward (LOCF).
prompt:
Industrial IoT sensors emit readings intermittently to save bandwidth. Downstream machine learning models require strict continuous 1-minute time grids with Last Observation Carried Forward (LOCF).

Execute the required analytical SQL calculation in DuckDB.
Expected output columns: bucket_time, device_id, raw_reading, filled_temperature.
Results should be ordered as specified.
golden_sql:
-- Resample sparse telemetry into continuous 1-minute intervals with Last Observation Carried Forward
            WITH time_grid AS (
                SELECT UNNEST(generate_series(
                    TIMESTAMP '2026-03-01 08:00:00',
                    TIMESTAMP '2026-03-01 08:05:00',
                    INTERVAL '1 minute'
                )) AS bucket_time
            ),
            aligned_readings AS (
                SELECT 
                    grid.bucket_time,
                    42 AS device_id,
                    st.temperature
                FROM time_grid grid
                LEFT JOIN sensor_telemetry st
                  ON grid.bucket_time = st.recorded_at
                 AND st.device_id = 42
            )
            SELECT 
                bucket_time,
                device_id,
                temperature AS raw_reading,
                -- Forward fill the most recent non-null temperature
                COALESCE(
                    temperature,
                    LAST_VALUE(temperature IGNORE NULLS) OVER (
                        PARTITION BY device_id 
                        ORDER BY bucket_time 
                        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
                    )
                ) AS filled_temperature
            FROM aligned_readings
            ORDER BY bucket_time;
why_it_fails: Using OUTER JOIN without dynamic range generation leaves temporal voids, leading to missing periods in downstream feature stores.
